analysis.investment_thesis: Aegis Vopak is a high-quality India energy infrastructure play — a JV between Aegis Logistics and Royal Vopak — riding the structural tailwind of LPG imports and chemical storage demand, with 86.94% promoter holding and 48% operating margins. However, at 109x P/E and 55x EV/EBITDA with only 8.73% ROE, the price embeds a decade of flawless execution; I would wait for better entry.
key_strengths: Asset-heavy terminalling moat with expanding capacity; revenue 353→621 Cr (76% in 2Y) and FY25 FCF flipped positive to +350 Cr
Blue-chip promoter pair (Aegis + Royal Vopak) owning 86.94%; post-IPO deleveraging cut borrowings from 3,273 to 2,004 Cr
Structural India tailwind — rising LPG imports, PCPIR chemical storage demand, and strategic port-side assets with long 10+ year runway
key_risks: Valuation is extreme — 109x trailing, 42x forward P/E, 31x P/S for a capital-intensive utility-like business
ROE just 8.73% and ROCE 7.01% — below my 15% threshold and barely covering cost of capital given 193 Cr finance costs
Heavy capex cycle with 1,786 Cr investing outflow in FY23 — growth depends on executing future terminal buildouts on time and yield
red_flags: P/E above 40x threshold with no exceptional moat to justify it
Returns (ROE/ROCE) well below cost of equity for a new listing priced for perfection
analysis.detailed_analysis: This is exactly the kind of India infrastructure story I love philosophically — energy logistics is a decade-long structural bet, LPG consumption is going only one way, and having Royal Vopak (the global terminalling leader) as a co-promoter alongside Aegis is a rare quality signal for Indian markets. Revenue grew from 353 Cr to 621 Cr in two years, operating margins are 48%, and the company just turned FCF positive at 350 Cr while deleveraging borrowings by ~1,270 Cr post-IPO. Promoter holding of 86.94% and limited governance worries make this a respectable franchise.\n\nBut the Big Bull does not overpay. 109x trailing P/E and 42x forward on a business earning 8.73% ROE is a mismatch — in infrastructure you need either dominant scale-driven returns or a margin-of-safety price, and this has neither today. EV/EBITDA of 56x prices in aggressive capacity additions going perfectly for the next 5–7 years; any execution hiccup or delay on new terminals will compress the multiple violently. I'd put this on the watchlist, let lock-in expiries and the inevitable post-listing volatility play out, and accumulate closer to 25–30x EV/EBITDA when reality reprices the stock. Good business, wrong price — HOLD.
